Hello! Last year I got a commission from you that I was very happy with. I'd like to get a followup in your style. Specifically, I'd like to get the same character in a few different poses with various faces. The goal is for the drawings to look like character reactions in a visual novel!

I've increased the payment to account for the amount of work I'm about to describe, but if anything I'm describing sounds like it would be a bit too much work, please feel free to scale back to the amount of work appropriate for the amount I've given!

Anywhere from 3 to 9 poses would be nice, with a few different facial expressions for each! I appreciate the inclusion of the photoshop file so I can choose different layers and tweak them personally, which will also help with this.

For poses, these could be basic gestures on a simple body. Things like folding her arms, looking away, hands on hips, etc. It could also be more complex poses, like leaning forward, stretching out, sitting down, looking bashful, etc. I have no preference for any of these, and I trust your judgement more than my own! Any pose that you feel would fit well. Please feel free to follow your instinct, or if you prefer instruction you can use my examples.

For expressions, I suppose they'd have to at least be somewhat related to the poses they're on. Using the "stretching out" pose as an example, she could have a happy celebratory face, a strained face, a relaxed expressionless face, etc. Again, I support you following your artistic instinct here. If nothing else, basic expressions like "happy, sad, angry, blushing, lovestruck, neutral" are also okay.

I think keeping with a single outfit would be best, as if there were inconsistencies between outfits in different poses, putting them in sequence would look awkward, and I feel that having multiple different outfit drawn for each of the poses, on top of the faces, would be asking too much of you. For that reason, one outfit is enough.

As for the character design itself, I already really like how you draw her! That said, I have a few notes about her design that I think are important, which you can see examples of in the references included.

First, is her general atmosphere. She's actually a bit awkward! I'd even call her sort of creepy, but in a charming way. Good characters to reference for this would be:
- Hex Maniac from Pokemon
- Kuroki Tomoko from Watamote
- Hyouka Fuwa from Shimoneta
- Ieiri Shoko from Jujutsu Kaisen
- Koumori Kuroko from Murcielago.
I think simple things like giving her a wider smile and eye bags should be enough!

Second, her maturity. I feel like you drew her somewhat young looking, almost like a teenager. She's a young adult, but she's nearing 30, so she's a bit taller, a bit wider, and her face is slightly more defined. "Handsome" might be a good word for it. The reference images will be very helpful here!

Speaking of reference images, I'd like to explain how I arranged them. At the very top is the original commission! I like the brush you used, and I like how sharp your angles are! Right below your drawing, is a self portrait that I drew of myself. I'm not sure if you recall from the first commission, but the character is a stand-in for me! I feel quite good about how accurately the self portrait I drew reflects how I look in real life, so it should be helpful (though I was a bit too modest with my boobs to be honest). Below that, all of the drawings of the character descend based on how faithful they are to the design. Even as they become slightly more cartoonish, they all capture the essence of the character!

So, to summarize:
- Visual novel poses
- 3-9 poses total
- A few different expressions for each pose, however much makes sense to you
- Slightly creepier
- Slightly more tired
- Slightly more mature

Also, for the record, I don't actually plan to make a visual novel using these, I mostly use them for when I post on my blog!

Thank you so much, I hope to hear back from you!
